record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: continuity of minimizers of relaxed harmonic-map energy
record.original_question: For the relaxed energy R on H^1_g(Omega; S^2), defined by weak H^1 limits of continuous competitors in the B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map problem, minimizers of R exist. Are all minimizers of R continuous on the closed ball, or at least does there exist one minimizer of R that is continuous on the closed ball?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 ([2]). Are the minimizers of (4.9) continuous on closed Omega? (Is it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth boundary datum. Denote
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u| = 1 \text{ a.e.}, \ u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}.$$
Let $C^0_g(\overline\Omega; S^2)$ denote the subclass of maps in $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ that are continuous on $\overline\Omega$. The Dirichlet energy is
$$E(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx.$$
Because $C^0_g(\overline\Omega; S^2)$ is in general not sequentially weakly $H^1$-dense in $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$, define the relaxed energy on $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ by
$$R(u) = \inf\left\{ \liminf_{k\to\infty} E(u_k) : u_k \in C^0_g(\overline\Omega; S^2),\ u_k \rightharpoonup u \text{ weakly in } H^1\right\}.$$
It is known that the infimum of $R$ over $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ is attained.

Question: Is every minimizer $u^*$ of $R$ continuous on $\overline\Omega$? If not, does there exist at least one minimizer of $R$ that is continuous on $\overline\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: Bethuel–Brezis–Coron and subsequent work (e.g., Hardt–Lin–Poon, Giaquinta–Modica–Souček) established that minimizers of the relaxed energy are smooth away from a finite (or small) singular set, but the question of full continuity up to the closed ball — or even existence of a single continuous minimizer — does not appear to have been resolved in the literature. Recent works on relaxed harmonic map energies continue to treat the regularity/continuity of relaxed minimizers as an open issue.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of minimizers of relaxed problems for harmonic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Every minimizer of the relaxed energy is smooth except at a finite number of points.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial regularity result; continuity on the closed ball is not established.

status_evidence.title: On the minimizers of the relaxed energy functional of mappings from higher dimensional balls into S^2
status_evidence.snippet: Partial regularity theorems have been proven for minimizers of the relaxed energy functional, with singularities described via minimal connections.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial regularity is known; full continuity remains unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Relaxed Energies for Harmonic Maps (Bethuel–Brezis–Coron)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces the relaxed energy R and studies properties of its minimizers.
status_evidence.claim: Original framework where the continuity question was raised.
